descriptionChirho: A moth or moth-larva, a small insect whose larvae consume fabric and organic material; used figuratively of the slow, insidious destruction wrought by God or by the passage of time (Job 4:19, 13:28, 27:18, Hos 5:12, Isa 50:9, 51:8, Psa 39:12). Multilingual evidence consistently identifies this as moth: eng 'moth/the moth/like a moth,' spa 'polilla/como polilla,' hin 'kiiraa/patange/ke jaise kiire,' arb 'uthth/suus/ka-l-uthth,' kor 'jom-i/jom/jwa-gati,' swa 'nondo/kama nondo.' The prepositional and article-prefixed forms represent syntactic variation (comparison 'like a moth'), not a distinct meaning.
